Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. The umpires return to the park along with the Australian openers, Travis Head and David Warner stride out to the middle. Bangladesh are in a huddle near the boundary before they spread onto the field. It will be the off-spin of Mahedi Hasan with the ball in hand for Bangladesh. Here we go!
…THE RUN CHASE…
UPDATE - 7.57 am IST (2.27 am GMT) - Good news folks! The rain has eased away and the covers are off. We should resume in a short while from now.

Right then, Australia needs 141 for the victory and start their Super 8s campaign on a winning note. How soon can they do it or will Bangladesh spring in a surprise? We shall find out. Join us in a bit for the second essay. Oh No! It has started to drizzle in Antigua and the covers are on. Let's hope this is a passing shower and we can resume quickly. Stay tuned for all the updates!

Adam Zampa is in for a chat. He says that having played here last week, they knew what to expect. Adds that the wicket is slightly different than last time. Shares that the ball is coming out of his hand nicely and he has the full backing from the captain. Says that he is happy to have restricted Bangladesh to 140 and feels that this is definitely a gettable total.

For Australia, Pat Cummins and Adam Zampa were the stand-out bowlers with five wickets among them. Starc, Stoinis, and Maxwell chipped in with one apiece. Australia will be the happier side going into the break. They bowled tight lines and kept chipping away with wickets at crucial stages of the game and did not allow Bangladesh to score easy runs. The bowlers have done their job and the onus will now be on their batting unit to chase this down.

An outstanding bowling display from Australia has restricted Bangladesh to 140 for 8 in their 20 overs. Having sent into bat first, Bangladesh lost Tanzid Hasan in the first over but their skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto and Litton Das added 58 for the second wicket. Das looked scratchy while Shanto made a sublime 41. Bangladesh kept losing wickets at regular intervals and failed to build partnerships in the middle. Only Towhid Hridoy with 40 off 28 hung around in the middle and stuck some lusty blows to take his side to the 140-run mark.

Goes full and it is on off, Tanzim Hasan Sakib clears his front leg and swings through the line. Gets a thickish outside edge that flies down to deep third for just a single. Bangladesh finish with 140 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks break! The move to send Rishad Hossain up the order did not quite work out there for Bangladesh. This has been a sedate start from them but they have firepower left in the shed to accelerate in the second half of their batting effort. As for Australia, they have been disciplined with their lines and lengths and have not given much away. They will look to continue in the same fashion and chip away at the wickets as Bangladesh aim to up the ante. Towhid Hridoy is the new batter in. Also, it will be Mitchell Starc to bowl after the break.

Commentary.Commentary: Pat Cummins comes into the attack.
Serves it on a length, around off, Litton Das creams the drive but fails to get it past cover. A much-needed productive over for Bangladesh, 10 runs off it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Mitchell Starc to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Oh, that was not far away! Starc gets a steep bounce off a hard length, on off, Litton Das looks to play it late but gets a thickish outside edge that flies towards short third. David Warner flings himself to his left but fails to get any hand on it and it races away for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Mitchell Starc to Litton Das, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Looks to go full but it comes out as a low full toss, on off, Litton Das uses his feet and drives it between cover and mid off for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Mitchell Starc to Litton Das, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Litton Das finally gets one away! Starc bangs it into the deck, on off, Litton Das gets this one at a good height for the pull shot. The ball holds in the surface slightly and Das gets this one off the bottom half of the bat. However, it is enough to clear mid-wicket for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Mitchell Starc to Litton Das, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Das is struggling big time here. 2 runs off just 14 balls. Lands it on a good length, a hint of inward shape, on middle, Litton Das pushes it back to the bowler with a straight bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Mitchell Starc to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Dishes it out at the stumps, full in length, Litton Das closes the bat face early to work it on the leg side but gets a soft leading edge that rolls to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Mitchell Starc to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller in length and going across the left-hander, Najmul Hossain Shanto lunges to go for the drive but toe-ends his shot to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Josh Hazlewood to Najmul Hossain Shanto, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bends his back and digs it in short, on off, Najmul Hossain Shanto swivels in the crease and drags the pull straight to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Josh Hazlewood to Najmul Hossain Shanto, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: In the corridor of off, on a good length, Litton Das premeditates again as he shuffles across to the off side to execute the scoop. Gets an inside edge onto the pads on the off side for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Josh Hazlewood to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Hazlewood strays down leg, on a back of a length, Litton Das moves to the off side to play the scoop but fails to get any bat on it. Wide given.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Josh Hazlewood to Litton Das, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Slanting in, on the sixth stump line, on a hard length, Litton Das gets on top of the bounce and punches it to cover-point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Josh Hazlewood to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: At 137.7 kph, angling across, on a short of a good length, on off, Najmul Hossain Shanto stays leg side of the ball and works it in front of short third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Josh Hazlewood to Najmul Hossain Shanto, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! First six of the night! Hazlewood bowls it on a length from over the wicket, on off, Najmul Hossain Shanto backs away early and uses his feet to thump it back over mid on for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Josh Hazlewood to Najmul Hossain Shanto, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Quick single taken! Much fuller and it is around off, Najmul Hossain Shanto drills it back towards the bowler. Starc gets a hand on it in his follow through and takes the sting out of the ball. It rolls in front of mid off and the batters sneak in a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Mitchell Starc to Najmul Hossain Shanto, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Litton Das is finally off the mark! Drags the length back and bowls it closer to the off-stump line, Litton Das hangs back and dabs it down to deep third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Mitchell Starc to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: 9 balls without a run on the board for Litton Das. Offers width this time, fuller as well, Litton Das reaches out and caresses the drive but it goes straight to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Mitchell Starc to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Missed out! It was there to be put away for Litton Das. Starc looks to go full again but dishes out a low full toss, angling across, Litton Das gives himself room and drives but hits it straight to the man at cover-point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Mitchell Starc to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Litton Das has faced 7 balls but he is yet to open his account. Angling away from the right-hander, very full, on off, Litton Das squeezes it out to backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Mitchell Starc to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hurls it in on a fullish length, on off and middle, Najmul Hossain Shanto pushes it to the right of mid on and calls Das through for a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Mitchell Starc to Najmul Hossain Shanto, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Goes searching for that magical delivery but gets the line wrong. Slips it down leg for a wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Mitchell Starc to Najmul Hossain Shanto, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: And again! Bangs it into the wicket, on off, Litton Das has no room to work with and can only push this one back to the bowler with a straight bat. Hazlewood starts with a maiden!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Josh Hazlewood to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bashes it on that hard length, slanting in, on off, Litton Das plays it right under his eyes as he punches it on the bounce to backward point. Make that five dots in a row.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Josh Hazlewood to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Goes fuller this time at 133.6 kph, outside off, Litton Das gets a good stride in and knocks it firmly to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Josh Hazlewood to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Puls the length back even more and keeps it over off, Litton Das hops back and pats along the ground to cover. Three dots to start with.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Josh Hazlewood to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Delivers it in the channel on off, on a back of a length again, Litton Das pushes and the ball pings off his bat but can't get it past backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Josh Hazlewood to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angling in, on a back of a length, over middle and leg, Litton Das rides the bounce and blocks it out on the leg side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Josh Hazlewood to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Who will bowl from the other end? It will be Josh Hazlewood.
FOUR! Flayed away! Starc errs in line and length as this is short and wide on off, Najmul Hossain Shanto frees his arms and slaps it up and over backward point for the first boundary of the game.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Mitchell Starc to Najmul Hossain Shanto, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and swinging away, at the stumps, Najmul Hossain Shanto gets right behind the line of the ball and plays it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Mitchell Starc to Najmul Hossain Shanto, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Drags the length back a touch but the late away shape is still there, on middle and leg, Najmul Hossain Shanto is watchful as he defends it out solidly with a straight bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Mitchell Starc to Najmul Hossain Shanto, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Najmul Hossain Shanto comes in at number 3.

OUT! DRAGGED ON! Mitchell Starc with the early strike for Australia! Stays over the wicket and targets the off pole, on a length and gets the ball to go away late from the left-hander. The ball skids through off the deck and it stays low as well. Tanzid Hasan stays rooted in his crease and tries to play the line of the ball with a straight bat. It catches the bottom edge of the bat and goes back onto hit the stumps.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Mitchell Starc to Tanzid Hasan, OUT! b Mitchell Starc.

Commentary.Commentary: Very full again and gets a hint of late away shape, at 139.3 kph, on off, Tanzid Hasan digs it out in front of cover from the crease.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Mitchell Starc to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Right on the money! Steams in from over the wicket and dishes out a yorker, swinging away, around the base of the off stump, Tanzid Hasan gets his bat down and jams it out square where Glenn Maxwell dives to his left to make the stop.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Mitchell Starc to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: The national anthems are done and dusted and we are all set for the action to commence. The two umpires make their way out to the middle as do Mitchell Marsh and his men. It will be Tanzid Hasan and Litton Das to open the innings for Bangladesh. Mitchell Starc will start with the new ball for Australia. Let's play...

Thankfully, we are starting on time, and we are moments away from the first ball in this clash, but before that, the match officials and the two sets of players will line up for the national anthems. It will be Bangladesh's national anthem first followed by the national anthem of Australia.

Najmul Hossain Shanto, the Bangladesh skipper says that he would have bowled first as well but is happy to bat. Shares that Mahedi Hasan comes in for Jaker Ali. Mentions that as a batting group, they need to do something special and step up.

The captain of Australia, Mitchell Marsh says that they will bowl first. Adds that this is a decent wicket and reckons that it won't change much throughout the 40 overs. Says that having played 1 game here at this venue, it is nice to get used to the conditions and hopes that they can have a good night. Informs that they have made two changes with Pat Cummins coming in for Ashton Agar and Josh Hazlewood replacing Nathan Ellis.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Tanzid Hasan, Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Litton Das (WK), Shakib Al Hasan, Towhid Hridoy, Mahmudullah, Rishad Hossain, Mahedi Hasan (In for Jaker Ali), Taskin Ahmed, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Mustafizur Rahman.

Australia (Playing XI) - Travis Head, David Warner, Mitchell Marsh (C), Glenn Maxwell, Marcus Stoinis, Tim David, Matthew Wade (WK), Pat Cummins (In for Ashton Agar), Mitchell Starc, Adam Zampa, Josh Hazlewood (In for Nathan Ellis).
TOSS - Australia have won the toss and they have elected to BOWL first.

UPDATE - 5.38 am IST (12.08 am GMT) - Good news! It has stopped raining and the covers are coming off. Considering the intensity of the rain that fell and that the players are already out there going through their warm-up drills, we should not be far away from the flip of the coin. Stay tuned.

UPDATE - 5.33 am IST (12.03 am GMT) - Uh, oh! It has started to rain out of nowhere and is concerning enough for the ground staff to cover the entire square. As a result, the toss has been delayed for now. There is a strong breeze blowing across, and let's hope it blows the rain away. Stick around for further updates.

Bangladesh, on the other hand, were in a group of death but managed to qualify with three wins from four outings. They won convincingly against the Netherlands but made it tough for themselves against Nepal and Sri Lanka. Their batters haven’t fired yet but the bowling has looked threatening. The likes of Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Mustafizur Rahman, Taskin Ahmed, and Rishad Hossain have been in fine form and can challenge any side on their given day. Bangladesh will look to be competitive and challenge Australia in all facets of the game. Can Bangladesh cause an upset or will Australia be too strong for them? Let’s find out. Toss and team news in a bit. Stay tuned!

Hello and a warm welcome to coverage of Match 4 in the Super 8 stage of the T20 World Cup, 2024. Australia are taking on Bangladesh at the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium in North Sound, Antigua. Australia played some brilliant cricket through the group stage and were undefeated in their four games. Marcus Stoinis has been in terrific form so far as the all-rounder has smashed over 150 runs in three outings and has stuck at over 190. With the ball, he has chipped in with key wickets. The likes of David Warner, Travis Head, and Tim David have been in good form but the Aussies will hope that Mitchell Marsh and Glenn Maxwell to fire. Adam Zampa has been the standout with the ball and the pace bowlers have supported him well. Australia looks like a well-oiled unit and will be favorite going into this contest but Bangladesh cannot be taken lightly.
…MATCHDAY…

The highly anticipated Super 8 stage of the ICC Men's T20 World Cup has arrived, and the teams are engaged in an intense battle for supremacy. The tournament has been a gripping spectacle thus far, with matches that have kept spectators on the edge of their seats, unfolding as nail-biting thrillers. The fourth match of the thrilling Super 8s stage sees the formidable Australian side gearing up to take on Bangladesh at the iconic Sir Vivian Richards Stadium in North Sound, Antigua. The Aussies have been in blistering form across formats lately, and they dominated the group stage, emerging unbeaten and maintaining a clean sheet with four consecutive victories under their belt. Australia's batting unit has been in scintillating form, and the presence of the explosive Travis Head at the top of the order has provided them with blistering starts right from the outset. Head's ability to take the game by the scruff of its neck in the powerplay overs has made him a deadly proposition for any bowling attack. David Warner’s form also holds a key to their success. They boast a power-packed batting lineup capable of making up for any shortcomings. Their skipper Mitchell Marsh leads from the front and is a formidable batter himself. Then there's the muscular Marcus Stoinis, who has been an absolute nightmare for bowlers, peppering them with disdain and clearing the ropes at will. While their middle order hasn't quite fired on all cylinders yet, Australia has players like the mercurial Glenn Maxwell who is tailor-made for the big stage. Maxwell is not just a batting maverick but also a serious component with the ball, capable of complementing the other spin wizards like Adam Zampa and Ashton Agar. Speaking of Zampa, he has been incredibly miserly, barely giving anything away to the opposition batters with his frugal spells. And as always, the Australian pace attack sends shivers down the spine of the opposition batters, and nothing less would be anticipated from Mitchell Starc and others. Bangladesh secured their Super 8s berth on the back of a thrilling, low-scoring victory against Nepal, where they successfully defended a modest total. Their runs have primarily come from Towhid Hridoy's bat, and they'll need others to step up. Skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto's underwhelming form with the bat has been a concern, and the side will be hoping for a strong comeback from their skipper as they've struggled for solid starts up front. The team will also be counting on Litton Das to rediscover his touch with the bat. The hard-hitting batter has struggled to make an impact so far, with just one score above single digits in the tournament. The experienced duo of Shakib Al Hasan and Mahmudullah provide valuable all-round skills to Bangladesh's middle order, capable of bailing them out in crunch situations. While the batting has underwhelmed, Tanzid Hasan Sakib has emerged as a lethal pace spearhead, consistently delivering with the ball. The spin department holds the key, with the impressive Rishad Hossain complementing the wily Shakib. While this clash will take place at Antigua, this spin duo could prove pivotal against the mighty Australians who have struggled a bit against the spin. While the venue recently witnessed a batting blitz from the West Indies and the score breaching beyond 200, this clash shapes up as an enthralling contest between Australia's formidable batting might and Bangladesh's bowling arsenal. With bat and ball expected to have an even say, this clash promises a thrilling nail-biter. Can Bangladesh's bowlers rise to the challenge, or will the rampant ‘Straaya’ continue their merry run and tighten their grip on the tournament? Only time will tell.
